what_it_is.prose: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is the apex R&D wing of India's Ministry of Defence, headquartered at Rajaji Marg, New Delhi. With approximately 50 laboratories spanning aeronautics, armaments, electronics, land combat, naval systems, life sciences, materials, missiles, and micro-electronics, DRDO is the principal designer of India's strategic and tactical defence systems. DRDO is not a commercial manufacturer; its technologies are transferred to BEL, BDL, BrahMos Aerospace, HAL, and private OEMs via Transfer of Technology (ToT) frameworks. Flagship programmes include the Agni and Prithvi strategic missile series, the Akash Surface-to-Air Missile family (with BEL and BDL as productionisers), the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft (with HAL and Aeronautical Development Agency), the BrahMos cruise missile (a JV with Russia's NPOM, 50.5% DRDO / 49.5% NPOM), the Pinaka Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher, the ATAGS towed artillery gun (with KSSL/Bharat Forge and TASL), the Arjun Main Battle Tank, the AEW&C airborne early warning system, the AMCA 5th-generation fighter programme, the Astra BVRAAM, and the Nag ATGM. In counter-UAS, DRDO designed the D4 Counter Drone System and its successor, the Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System (IDDIS) — Atlas slug cus-001 — produced by BEL. DRDO's CHESS laboratory has issued an Expression of Interest for ToT of its 30 kW Laser DEW System to three Indian industry partners. At Aero India 2025 on 11 February 2025, DRDO and Adani Defence & Aerospace unveiled a Vehicle-Mounted Counter-Drone System under a ToT framework.

deployments_procurement.summary: DRDO is funded via the union budget (Defence R&D capital and revenue allocations) rather than commercial revenue. Its technologies reach Indian armed forces through ToT to BEL, BDL, HAL, BrahMos Aerospace, and private OEMs. Major DRDO-designed systems in operational service include the Agni and Prithvi strategic missile series (with Strategic Forces Command), Akash SAM (Indian Army and IAF, ~₹30,000+ crore in aggregate orders across BEL/BDL), BrahMos (multi-domain, ~₹30,000+ crore cumulative), Pinaka MBRL (7 regiments operational, target 22 long-term), Tejas LCA (40 delivered, 180 more on order), Arjun MBT Mk-1A (118 ordered, ₹6,500 crore), and ATAGS (307 guns ordered March 2025, ₹6,900 crore). In counter-UAS, IDDIS has been in operational service since March 2024 with the Indian Army, with combat use confirmed in Operation Sindoor (May 2025).

import_dependencies.summary: DRDO is the apex R&D body and the principal indigenisation driver. However, laboratory-scale dependencies include test equipment (oscilloscopes, RF sources — USA / Germany), specialty materials (composites, titanium alloys, single-crystal turbine blades — USA / Japan / Russia) for Tejas/Kaveri/AMCA programmes, FPGA and GaN for radar/EW prototypes (same global supply chain as BEL — USA), and seeker components for BrahMos (Russia NPOM, legacy).

faq.question: Is DRDO a commercial manufacturer?
faq.answer: No. DRDO is the R&D wing of India's Ministry of Defence, funded via the union budget. It is not a commercial entity and does not report revenue, profit, or an order book. DRDO-designed systems reach Indian armed forces through Transfer of Technology (ToT) to productionisers such as BEL, BDL, HAL, BrahMos Aerospace, and private OEMs like TASL, L&T, and KSSL/Bharat Forge.

faq.question: Which DRDO labs lead counter-UAS work?
faq.answer: Counter-UAS R&D at DRDO is led by five laboratories: CHESS (Centre for High Energy Systems and Sciences, Hyderabad — laser DEW), LASTEC (Laser Science and Technology Centre, Delhi — laser source), LRDE (Electronics and Radar Development Establishment, Bengaluru — radar), DLRL (Defence Electronics Research Lab, Hyderabad — EW and SIGINT), and IRDE (Instruments Research and Development Establishment, Dehradun — EO/IR).

faq.question: How is DRDO organised and how many labs does it have?
faq.answer: DRDO has approximately 50 laboratories across India spanning aeronautics, armaments, electronics, land combat, naval systems, life sciences, materials, missiles, and micro-electronics. Key laboratories involved in counter-UAS work include CHESS (Centre for High Energy Systems and Sciences, Hyderabad — laser DEW), LASTEC (Laser Science and Technology Centre, Delhi — laser source), LRDE (Electronics and Radar Development Establishment, Bengaluru — radar), DLRL (Defence Electronics Research Lab, Hyderabad — EW and SIGINT), and IRDE (Instruments Research and Development Establishment, Dehradun — EO/IR).
